title: Polynomial-Time Encoding of Acceptance Constraints
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, and let $n,s,o:\{0,1	ext{-strings}	o\mathbb N\}$ be functions such that each of the three maps $x\mapsto 1^{n(x)}$, $x\mapsto 1^{s(x)}$, and $x\mapsto 1^{o(x)}$ is computable by $M$-model polynomial time. Then the map sending $x$ to the binary encoding of the acceptance CNF for parameters $n(x),s(x)$, with every variable index shifted by $o(x)$, is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state Turing machine over Boolean symbols
$n,s,o$ map Boolean strings to natural numbers
